title: Public state documentation audit

context.summary: Update public-facing docs so they accurately describe the current runnable demo state, supported surfaces, experimental paths, placeholders and future work after TASK-63.
context.background: README and deployment docs still contain older skeleton-era wording. Installer, document pipeline and production hardening docs need a clearer supported/experimental/future split before public release work continues.

in: Update README.md repository status and local demo quickstart.
Update docs/DEPLOYMENT.md to describe current Compose/demo support and experimental profiles.
Update docs/INSTALLER.md to make current dry-run versus future execution boundaries explicit.
Update docs/DOCUMENT_PIPELINE.md to separate supported fallback processing from future model-backed processing.
Update docs/PRODUCTION_HARDENING.md to distinguish current baseline from public release gaps.

acceptance_criteria: README.md no longer claims the repository is only bootstrapped through TASK-53.
Docs clearly distinguish supported, experimental, placeholder/profile-smoke and future capabilities.
Local demo quickstart documents pnpm mvp:demo, mvp:up, mvp:reset and pnpm check.
Installer docs state that current CLI is dry-run/planning and full execution is a later task.
Document pipeline docs state which modality processors are deterministic fallback versus model-backed future work.
Production hardening docs identify GitHub/public-release gaps without implying they are already complete.

commands: rg -n "TASK-53|Fastify API skeleton|Docker Compose placeholders|profile skeleton" README.md docs/DEPLOYMENT.md docs/INSTALLER.md docs/DOCUMENT_PIPELINE.md docs/PRODUCTION_HARDENING.md
manual_checks: Confirm docs do not overstate unsupported model-backed or installer execution behavior.

risks: Docs may accidentally market deterministic fallback behavior as real model-backed processing.
Docs may imply the installer mutates host state before the executor task exists.
definition_of_done: Task status is changed to accepted or done.
Branch is committed and merged back into master.
